A Limitations
While our method can train the model to focus on diverse regions within an image, it does not
allow explicit control over where each attention head focuses, as the regions of focus are determined
implicitly during training. As a result, it is not possible to know in advance which regions each
attention head will focus on until after training. Our method also increases the training time and
introduces a trade-off between classification performance and performance improvements in zero-shot
segmentation, object discovery, and FOIR tasks. Exploring other effective ways to utilize the visual
focusing image representations obtained by our method remains an important direction for future
work.

evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Self-distillation cross-entropy losses between student and teacher representations, where the student output is modified by prompt-guided attention head selection using randomly sampled crop and mask boxes without ground-truth semantic annotations.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: The empirical findings support the claimed trade-offs and improvements, showing consistent gains in dense zero-shot localization and spatial diversity alongside an acknowledged slight reduction in single-label global classification accuracy.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation thoroughly tests the claimed emergent spatial specialization across multiple independent standard benchmarks, including zero-shot segmentation (ImageNet-Seg, PASCAL VOC), unsupervised object discovery (LOST on VOC07, VOC12, COCO), image retrieval, and supervised semantic segmentation (ADE20k, Cityscapes, VOC). Ablations on loss weights, head selection counts, entropy metrics, and continual learning validate the mechanism.

primary.limitations: The authors transparently report the lack of explicit deterministic control over which head attends where, increased training overhead, and the slight degradation in k-NN and linear classification performance on ImageNet.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is explicitly defined, modifying self-distillation (DINOv2) by pairing cropped and masked teacher views with prompt-guided head-selected student outputs. Full training hyperparameters, architecture variations (ViT-B, ViT-L, ViT-g with registers), ablation settings, and loss formulations are clearly documented.
primary.quality_rationale: The study provides clear methodological definitions, extensive empirical evaluations across diverse tasks and model sizes, and rigorous baselines with honest reporting of trade-offs, satisfying quality standards.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces two visual focusing loss functions (inside-focus and outside-focus) based on prompt-guided attention head selection for self-supervised Vision Transformers to encourage spatial attention head specialization and improve dense visual representation tasks without human annotations.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: The reported experimental numbers substantiate the scoped claims, demonstrating competitive detection performance (0.561 NDS and 0.459 mAP on nuScenes val) and confirming the functional specialization of the sliced physical representations via ablation and intervention experiments.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluation is conducted on the standard nuScenes 3D detection benchmark against established baselines (StreamPETR, Sparse4D, BEVNeXt) reporting official metrics including NDS, mAP, and TP errors. Detailed ablation studies isolate the contributions of channel slicing, explicit prior propagation, fusion variants, latency/memory footprint, and feature-slice zeroing interventions.

primary.limitations: The authors clearly acknowledge the computational and latency overhead introduced by the additional encoders and modulation modules, the reliance on the shared slice for contextual reasoning, and the need for deeper attribute disentanglement.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing the channel partitioning into shared and attribute slices (center, dimension, orientation, velocity), complex-valued positional encodings for angles, ego-motion transformation of physical priors, soft semantic prior construction, and mutual gated affine modulation with stored implicit instance queries.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents a clear, well-formulated technical contribution with clear motivation, comprehensive mathematical descriptions, solid empirical validation on standard benchmarks, and insightful ablation studies.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces ExQuery, a camera-based temporal 3D object detection framework that structures object queries into shared semantic-context and physical-state-specific slices, maintaining this attribute alignment through prior encoding, branch-specific regression, and ego-motion temporal propagation with mutual gated affine modulation.
